The first of four days on where returns come from, and the only one of the four whose source is compensation for bearing something rather than skill at anything.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Name four distinct risk premia and, for each, the bad state of the world in which it loses money.
- Give the historical equity risk premium in the US with a standard error attached, and say why that standard error is larger than people behave as though it is.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Read the free chapter 1 of Ilmanen's Investing Amid Low Expected Returns. It is the most careful public account of what expected returns are and how badly they are estimated.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Estimate it yourself from the Ken French monthly market excess return series, over the full sample: annualised mean, annualised volatility, and the standard error of the mean. Then compute how many years of data you would need for a 2 percentage point standard error. The answer is the reason this is hard.
:::
:::
